one_liner: Rust crate with its own HTTP/2 and gRPC stack. Its unary gRPC server served 3.7-5.5x grpc-go's req/s on HttpArena.
what_it_does: wtx is one Rust crate that implements gRPC, HTTP/2 with HPACK, TLS 1.3, WebSocket, a PostgreSQL client and other protocols itself, each turned on by a Cargo feature. The gRPC server (feature grpc-server) is a thin layer over wtx's own HTTP/2 server framework. You register each method path by hand in an HttpRouter with GrpcMiddleware. A handler decodes the request with GrpcManager::des_from_req_bytes and writes the reply with ser_to_res_bytes. It is not a drop-in replacement: it supports only unary calls, generates no service code from .proto files, and expects message types from a third-party protobuf generator such as quick-protobuf/pb-rs.
how_it_is_fast: Http2ServerFramework::run_in_threads uses a runtime-per-thread, shared-nothing design. It starts one single-threaded tokio LocalRuntime per available thread. Each runtime binds its own listener (SO_REUSEPORT is on by default) and runs its connection and stream tasks locally, so the hot path has no work-stealing and no cross-thread handoff. The HTTP/2 framing, HPACK and Huffman code are written in-house, and the response is built in the same buffer as the request, so a reply no larger than the request needs no new allocation. The benchmark binary also used target-cpu=native, thin LTO, codegen-units=1, panic=abort and wtx's optimizations-std feature (memchr, simdutf8, socket2).
when_to_use: A Rust service whose hot path is small unary gRPC calls at very high request rates on a many-core Linux box. On HttpArena, wtx served 3.99M req/s against grpc-go's 0.72M with 256 h2c connections.

Workloads with hundreds to thousands of connections, each carrying many concurrent streams. These spread well across the per-thread listeners; the benchmark used 256-1024 connections with 100 streams each.
gRPC over TLS without a separate TLS stack: in HttpArena's unary-grpc-tls test, with wtx's own TLS 1.3, it reached 3.69M vs 0.70M req/s (256 connections) and 3.63M vs 0.93M (1024).
Internal services, prototypes or benchmark rigs where you control the .proto files and both ends, and you can type the service routes by hand.

Projects that want gRPC, HTTP/2, WebSocket and Postgres from one crate with a small dependency tree and fast builds. The README reports 2 required dependencies and a 6.53 s clean optimized build for the gRPC client.
when_not_to_use: You need server, client or bidirectional streaming RPCs. The gRPC module supports unary calls only.

You need generated service stubs or the usual gRPC ecosystem. Services must be typed by hand; the macro for this is still open issue #231. Reflection, health checking and interceptor libraries are not documented.

Production or security-sensitive systems. The README says wtx has had no security audit. In issue #452 (Nov 2025) the author calls it 'a fun project developed in my free-time that probably shouldn't be used in production' and advised a user to stay on tokio-tungstenite.

Small CPU budgets or strict tail-latency targets. In grpc_bench's 2026-04-23 run (wtx 0.40, 1-4 server CPUs, 1000 clients), wtx trailed go_grpc (93,004 vs 117,082 req/s at 4 CPUs) and tonic, and its p90 stayed at about 42 ms. On HttpArena its p99 was 69.93 ms at 256 connections (average 6.55 ms), and it used 727 MiB of memory against grpc-go's 310.5 MiB.
Teams that require stable Rust or a stable API. lib.rs enables nightly features, and crates.io lists 7 breaking minor releases (0.46 to 0.52) between 2026-05-16 and 2026-08-10.

integration.dependencies: For the benchmarked gRPC server: tokio, quick-protobuf, hashbrown, foldhash, plus memchr, simdutf8 and socket2 through optimizations-std. pb-rs (or another generator) is needed at build time to generate message types. TLS or other crypto needs one backend feature: crypto-ring (ring), crypto-alr (aws-lc-rs), crypto-graviola or crypto-ruco (RustCrypto).
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly only. lib.rs uses #![feature(random, return_type_notation)] even though crates.io lists rust-version 1.96. The repo pins nightly-2026-09-03, the crate uses edition 2024, and HttpArena built wtx 0.49 with nightly-2026-06-27.
integration.platforms: The core is no_std + alloc, and the README says it works on embedded devices with a heap allocator. Targets with 16-bit pointers are not supported. The multi-threaded server needs std; the executors are tokio, wtx's own std executor, and embassy-net. Benchmarks exist only for x86-64 Linux.
integration.thread_safety: run_in_threads gives each thread its own single-threaded runtime and its own clone of the application data, and each stream gets another clone. Shared mutable state must therefore live behind Arc or atomics inside that data. Http2ServerFramework::run, on a multi-threaded runtime, requires Send + Sync bounds. For TLS, the docs leave coordination between the concurrent reader and writer to the user.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it follows the gRPC over HTTP/2 wire spec, so standard gRPC clients over h2c or TLS+ALPN should work, but it is a Rust library with a different, unary-only, hand-routed server API rather than a replacement for grpc-go code

gotchas: The response is built in the request buffer, and the handler's return type decides what happens to that buffer. ResFinalizer for () (and for &str, String and Vector) calls req.clear(). A handler that writes its reply into req.msg_data.body and returns () therefore sends an empty body with grpc-status 0. This bug invalidated wtx's own HttpArena entry until PR #1300; return StatusCode or VerbatimParams instead.

If no crypto backend feature is selected, crypto calls panic or halt at runtime instead of failing the build. TLS and secure cookies need one of crypto-ring, crypto-alr, crypto-graviola or crypto-ruco.
HTTP/2 has no HTTP/1.1 Upgrade path. Clients must use prior-knowledge h2c or ALPN over TLS. Stream prioritization and server push are not supported.

The README warns that wtx assumes the summed length of any number of slices cannot overflow. On 32-bit targets, oversized input can overflow and cause unexpected behavior. The docs also flag PlaintextCtx (the TLS config used for plain h2c) as dangerous if misconfigured.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick wtx when the service is written in Rust and must keep standard gRPC-over-HTTP/2 clients: its measured gain over grpc-go (3.7-5.5x) is larger than that of Kitex (1.5-1.7x) or rpcx (2.3-2.6x), both Go, though each was measured on a different harness. grpcxx is the closest C++ analogue that also speaks gRPC; brpc is the more mature C++ multi-protocol choice.
verified_claims_summary: HttpArena ran a unary GetSum gRPC call over plaintext h2c, driven by h2load with 256 and 1024 connections, 100 streams each, 5 s runs, best of 3. The machine was a Threadripper PRO 3995WX, with the server pinned to 32 cores plus their SMT threads. wtx 0.49 (nightly Rust, target-cpu=native) served 3,990,708 req/s against grpc-go v1.72.0 (Go 1.24, default grpc.NewServer) at 720,798 req/s with 256 connections (5.5x). With 1024 connections it served 3,620,970 against 969,718 (3.7x). Two limits apply: wtx used about 64 logical CPUs against grpc-go's 44, and the two results come from different run dates (grpc-go on 2026-04-12, wtx re-validated on 2026-08-24).
status_note: Actively developed, almost entirely by one author (764 of about 790 non-bot commits; last commit 2026-09-08; 0.52.1 released 2026-08-14; about 70k crates.io downloads). The crate is MPL-2.0 and easy to depend on, but it is pre-1.0 with breaking releases every few weeks, nightly-only, unaudited, and its author does not recommend it for production.
